provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Love in action
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state ways to show love
The pupils should be able to demonstrate helping others
Introduction:
Last term we learned about being kind friends.
Today we learn how to show love with our actions.
Content:
Love in action means helping others without being asked.
When you see your friend carrying heavy books, help them.
When your teacher is tired, clean the blackboard.
We have a kindness jar in class.
When you see someone being kind, put a paper in the jar.
Class activity:
Let's play the helping game.
I will need a helper to carry these books.
Who wants to be the helper?
Evaluation questions:
What does love in action mean?
Name one way to show love at home.
Show me how you can help a friend.
Summary:
Love is shown when we help others without being asked.

topics.title: Self control
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify angry feelings
The pupils should be able to demonstrate calm tools
Introduction:
Everyone feels angry sometimes.
Today we learn how to control our anger.
Content:
Angry feelings are normal for everyone.
Even your teacher gets angry sometimes.
When you feel angry, use calm tools.
Breathe in slowly and breathe out.
Count to ten slowly.
Walk away from the angry situation.
These tools help you feel better.
Class activity:
Let's practice breathing together.
In through the nose, out through the mouth.
Now let's count to ten slowly.
Evaluation questions:
What are calm tools?
Show me how to breathe when angry.
What should you do when you feel angry?
Summary:
Use calm tools when you feel angry.

topics.title: Diligence
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain diligence
The pupils should be able to demonstrate finishing tasks
Introduction:
We all have small jobs to do.
Today we learn about doing our jobs well.
Content:
Diligence means finishing what you start.
If you start coloring a picture, finish it.
If you start cleaning your desk, finish it.
Little jobs done well make big differences.
Your teacher likes when you finish your work.
Class activity:
Let's practice diligence together.
Each of you will color half a picture.
Then we will switch and finish the other half.
Evaluation questions:
What does diligence mean?
Name one job you should finish.
Show me how you work diligently.
Summary:
Finish what you start with diligence.

topics.title: Contentment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state what contentment is
The pupils should be able to identify greed
Introduction:
Sometimes we want more toys or more snacks.
Today we learn about being happy with what we have.
Content:
Contentment means being happy with what you have.
When you have a pencil, be happy with it.
When you have one snack, be happy with it.
Greed steals joy because you always want more.
Greed makes you forget what you already have.
Class activity:
Let's play the happy game.
Show me your happy face with your snack.
Now show me your greedy face wanting more.
Which face feels better?
Evaluation questions:
What is contentment?
How does greed make you feel?
Name something you can be content with.
Summary:
Be happy with what you have.

topics.title: Courage
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to define courage
The pupils should be able to demonstrate standing up for others
Introduction:
Sometimes we feel scared to do the right thing.
Today we learn about being brave.
Content:
Courage means doing right even when you are afraid.
If someone is being bullied, be brave to tell a teacher.
If you see something wrong, be brave to speak up.
Standing up for others shows real courage.
Courage is not feeling no fear, but acting anyway.
Class activity:
Let's practice being brave.
I will pretend to bully this teddy bear.
Who will be brave to stand up for the teddy?
Evaluation questions:
What is courage?
Show me how you stand up for others.
Name a time you need courage.
Summary:
Be brave to do the right thing.

topics.title: Loyalty
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain loyalty
The pupils should be able to demonstrate keeping secrets
Introduction:
Good friends stay loyal to each other.
Today we learn about being loyal friends.
Content:
Loyalty means keeping safe secrets.
If your friend tells you a secret, keep it safe.\Loyalty means defending your friends' good name.
If someone says mean things about your friend, stand up for them.
Loyal friends trust each other.
Class activity:
Let's practice keeping secrets.
I will whisper a secret to each child.
Can you keep it safe?
Evaluation questions:
What does loyalty mean?
How do you keep a secret safe?
Show how you defend a friend.
Summary:
Be a loyal friend to others.

topics.title: Fairness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify fair behavior
The pupils should be able to demonstrate sharing and taking turns
Introduction:
Everyone likes to be treated fairly.
Today we learn about fairness in class and at home.
Content:
Fairness means sharing and taking turns.
When playing with toys, share them with others.
When using the computer, take turns with your friend.
Fairness means playing by the rules.
When playing games, follow the rules everyone agreed on.
Class activity:
Let's practice taking turns.
We will pass this ball around the circle.
Each child holds it for 5 seconds.
Evaluation questions:
What does fairness mean?
Show how you take turns.
Name one rule in our classroom.
Summary:
Be fair by sharing and following rules.

topics.title: Service to others
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list ways to serve others
The pupils should be able to demonstrate serving at home
Introduction:
We can help others in many ways.
Today we learn about serving others.
Content:
Service means helping others without being asked.
At home, you can help sweep the floor.
At home, you can help wash dishes.
In class, you can help clean the board.
In class, you can help organize books.
Being a helper makes you feel good.
Class activity:
Let's be helpers.
I need someone to help arrange these chairs.
Who wants to be the helper today?
Evaluation questions:
Name one way to serve at home.
Name one way to serve in class.
Show how you help others.
Summary:
Serve others by helping without being asked.

topics.title: Peace making
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain peace making
The pupils should be able to demonstrate solving quarrels
Introduction:
Sometimes friends argue and fight.
Today we learn how to make peace.
Content:
Peace making means being a bridge, not a bomb.
A bridge connects people, a bomb hurts people.
When friends quarrel, use words to solve problems.
Say "I'm sorry" when you do wrong.
Say "I forgive you" when someone apologizes.
Class activity:
Let's practice making peace.
Two children will pretend to quarrel.
Then we will practice saying sorry and forgiving.
Evaluation questions:
What does being a bridge mean?
How do you solve a quarrel with words?
Show how you say sorry.
Summary:
Make peace by using kind words.

topics.title: Revision and service awards
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall service stories
The pupils should be able to identify helpers
Introduction:
We have learned many ways to be good friends.
Today we remember all we learned and celebrate helpers.
Content:
We will share our service stories from this term.
Each child will tell one way they helped someone.
Then we will give service awards.
The helper of the term will get a special badge.
Being a helper makes our classroom better.
Class activity:
Let's share our service stories.
Sit in a circle and pass the talking stick.
When you have the stick, tell how you helped someone.
Evaluation questions:
What is one way you helped someone?
Who do you think is a helper in our class?
Show how you serve others.
Summary:
We all can be helpers and make peace.
